runs.text: With price-taking firms and no market failures, price equal to marginal cost gives allocative efficiency: the last unit's value equals its cost. Production at minimum average total cost (ATC) gives productive efficiency. Free entry and exit can deliver both in long-run competitive equilibrium.

rawReadingSequence: Outcome: Interpret Competitive Efficiency & Model Limits.

With price-taking firms and no market failures, price equal to marginal cost gives allocative efficiency: the last unit's value equals its cost. Production at minimum average total cost (ATC) gives productive efficiency. Free entry and exit can deliver both in long-run competitive equilibrium.
Allocative efficiency compares price with marginal cost.
Check whether private benefits and costs capture all social effects.
The competitive efficiency result assumes prices reflect social marginal benefits and costs. Externalities, market power, or incomplete information can break that connection.

At the long-run competitive outcome, the firm produces 50 units where price equals marginal cost and price also equals minimum ATC at $25. P = MC gives allocative efficiency, while production at minimum ATC gives productive efficiency. These conclusions depend on the competitive model's assumptions.
